about: THE DEAD ON THE MAP (WORLD 15 11/21; VAMILY rule 360, Paolo 11/3: 'we don't see enough corpses even throughout the world... billions of people have died', and its amendment the same round: 'if it's a busy civilized settlement or part of the town, obviously they don't have [corpses]... very simplified'). The one file a modder edits for where the dead lie on the map. Read by slices/bohemia_the_dead_on_the_map.js; the pictures are slices/map_dead/pieces.json (COOK DEAD's thirteen, tools/bohemia_world15_the_dead_on_the_map.py). Every number here is ours, draft, for TUNING's table.
from_tw_why: the dead lie on the ground the house models stand on: from a block 96 px (slices/bohemia_map_houses.js H.full), where a body is about 7 px, to the street stop (a block 380 px) where it is about 27; under that the valley is its towns and its roads
lift_why: drawn at twice their metres on the house models' own metre (TW / (sqrt 2 x 36)), the scale the map's men and houses stand at, so a body reads beside a 56 px man the way COOK DEAD's manifest asks (about 26 px at the near stop)
lived_why: rule 360(a): no bodies where people live and keep order: within this many blocks of a town's ground (every faction's base, his own outfit's), of a real place he can walk into, and of his home base, the living bury their dead: graves only there (grave_cross, grave_row; the pit stays, fenced)
never_why: COOK DEAD's body in a doorway brings its own storefront wall: alone on the map it is a box standing on a block (measured on the glass 11/21: two of them on a tower's face); it belongs against a real wall, on the fight boards
once_why: the pit (mass_grave) is one per place: never two within this many blocks

downtown.why: Fremont, the oldest camps: the sidewalks and the carts (COOK DEAD's downtown board)

strip.why: the casinos were the morgues; the tourists never left

trailer.why: the poorest parks in the valley

wash.why: the flood channels, the tunnel camps

works.why: the yards and the camps along the tracks

road.why: the streets between: a corner, its stop, a car that stopped

shops.why: a corner shop and its stop

flats.why: a dead block of flats, nobody left to bury

houses.why: where people lived they buried their own in the yards: graves, and the coat on the fence

mountain.why: the scenic loop, its cars still parked

graves.why: the fairways and the parks became the cemetery

school.why: the grave rows on the school fields

airport.why: the last flights that never came; the terminal was a clinic

clinic.why: a clinic that could not keep up
